name: Casella Waste Systems
notes: Researched from public casella.com pages (Pay Bill, Convenience Fees, Support, Residential Terms of Use) and the public My Account sign-in screen at mycasella.idoxs.net (Kubra; observed, never signed in). The Pay Bill page routes customers to a portal by state: Kubra My Account for DE/MD/ME/NJ/PA/VT (and some MA/NH/NY accounts by provider or account prefix), a separate Connecticut page and a Navusoft portal for West Virginia; this dossier models the Kubra My Account portal. Sign-in is Username + Password (reCAPTCHA protected) with Pay Now for a one-time payment. No Casella fee for paying online or by phone, but Kubra adds a 3.00% card convenience fee with a $1.50 minimum (not charged in CT and ME; the engine models the percentage only). Bank payments are free. Some markets charge a paper-bill fee (amount not published). Returned payments cost $25. Late fees/interest up to the legal limit (no amount). Start, stop or change service and payment plans/hardship go through Customer Care, not online. The autopay label is deliberately not set: the kubra template reuses that label as the text of its Turn off AutoPay link (see cross-owner request).

cancel_service.note: Service cannot be stopped online. Contact Casella Customer Care at 802-683-3984 (Mon-Fri 7am-5pm) to start, stop or change service.

payment_arrangement.note: Payment plans are not offered online. Contact Casella Customer Care before you miss a payment to discuss payment plans or hardship programs.

help.title: How do I pay my Casella bill?
paragraphs: Choose your state on the Pay Bill page to reach the right payment portal. Delaware, Maryland, Maine, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and Vermont customers use My Account; Massachusetts, New Hampshire and New York customers choose by provider or by the first two characters of the account number.

You can pay by credit or debit card or bank account (ACH) online, by phone, or by mailing a check. Casella charges nothing extra to pay online or by phone, and the portal is open around the clock. Bills are due on the date printed on them; late payments may bring a late fee or interest.
steps: Open Pay Bill and select your state.
Sign in to My Account, or choose Pay Now for a one-time payment.
Enter the amount and payment method.

help.title: Card convenience fee
paragraphs: Card payments through KUBRA, Casella's payment processor, carry a convenience fee of 3.00% per transaction with a $1.50 minimum. It applies to one-time and AutoPay card payments, is shown only on the KUBRA receipt and is generally not refundable.

Customers in Connecticut and Maine are not charged this fee. Paying from a bank account is free: existing users can add a bank account to their wallet and switch AutoPay to it. Some markets also charge a separate fee for paper bills.

help.title: AutoPay
paragraphs: Sign up for AutoPay in the secure payment portal so your bill is paid on time automatically. A bank account avoids the card convenience fee, which also applies to AutoPay card payments.

help.title: Payment plans and hardship
paragraphs: If you expect to miss a payment, contact Casella Customer Care beforehand to talk about payment plans or hardship programs. Call 802-683-3984 (Monday to Friday, 7 a.m. to 5 p.m.) or email; email replies can take 3 to 5 business days.

help.title: Start, stop or change service
paragraphs: To stop service, contact Casella Customer Care at 802-683-3984. Service is billed in advance; you pay the full monthly fee for the month you cancel and there are no refunds.
Casella collects its containers and may charge a reasonable removal fee; containers that are not returned may incur a replacement fee. A returned or rejected payment costs $25.

extra.intent: Using Casella's help pages, find the percentage and the minimum dollar amount of the convenience fee for paying by card. Do not make a payment or change any settings.

solution.text: Card payments carry a 3.00% convenience fee with a $1.50 minimum; bank payments are free.

extra.intent: Using Casella's help pages, find which two states' customers are not charged the card convenience fee. Do not make a payment or change any settings.

solution.text: Customers in Connecticut and Maine are exempt from the card convenience fee.
